### Observed differences

- Before, exactly one of A14, A15 and A20 ran in each case, late in the trace (mean relative position about 0.6): A14 in about 38 in 100 traces, A15 in about 32 and A20 in about 31. Each of the three was followed by A23 or A27 roughly half of the time, and A22 and A23 each led to one of the three in about half of their outgoing transitions. [POS001, POS002, POS003, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- In the later window, exactly one of the three still runs in each case (about 34, 35 and 32 in 100 for A14, A15, A20) but now early, at relative position about 0.3: A40, which previously always led to A21, now leads to A14, A15 or A20 (about one third each), each of the three always leads to A21, and A21 now follows A40 two steps later instead of immediately. [POS001, POS002, POS003, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR006, LAG004]
- The order between this block and A21/A22 flipped: before, A14, A15 and A20 came after A21 and after A22 in the roughly 31–38 in 100 traces where they co-occurred; in the later window they come before both. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]
- The late sequence became fixed: before, A22 was followed by A23 in about 48 in 100 of its outgoing transitions and A23 by A27 in about 53, with A27 three steps after A22; in the later window A22 is always followed by A23 and A23 always by A27, so A27 now comes two steps after A22. [DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]
- A10 and A11 still appear in every trace but repeat less often: mean occurrences per trace fell from about 1.9 to about 1.6, and the share of traces in which they recur fell from about 47 to about 38 in 100. [OCC001, OCC002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the alternative block A14/A15/A20 — exactly one of which executes per case — was relocated from the late stage of the process (between A22/A23 and A27) to the early stage (between A40 and A21). The change is shown directly on the relational and positional indicators: successor profiles reversed (A40 from always A21 to A14/A15/A20; A14/A15/A20 from A23/A27 to always A21; A22 and A23 from mixed successors to fixed ones), the order relative to A21 and A22 flipped from after to before, relative positions moved from about 0.6 to about 0.3 of the trace, and step distances changed consistently (A40→A21 from 1 to 2 steps, A22→A27 from 3 to 2). Participation of the three activities stayed essentially unchanged and still totals one execution per trace, which fits a move rather than activities being added or removed; with 24 qualifying items against roughly 0.39 expected by chance in a stable process, the pattern as a whole is not what sampling variation typically produces. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, POS001, POS002, POS003, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004]

Limitations: positions are event-based, so this shows a change in where the activities sit in the sequence, not a clock-time rescheduling. A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the late executions of A14/A15/A20 were removed and their early execution added as a separate insertion rather than a single relocation — behaviourally equivalent here, but not distinguishable from the logs. The small position shifts of A21, A22 and A23 (about 0.01–0.03 later) may simply be a side effect of the block now sitting earlier in the trace. [POS004, POS005, POS006]

Other differences: A10 and A11 occur in every trace in both windows but repeat less often in the later window (mean about 1.9 to about 1.6 occurrences per trace; recurrence in about 47 down to 38 in 100 traces) — a reduction in repetition that is not part of the relocation hypothesis. [OCC001, OCC002]
